title: Spec graph
no_project: Open a project to see its spec findings.
now_hint: Every deterministic finding at the project's branch: traceability, links and anchors, superseded decisions, the repository's own rules. These may gate a pull request.
stored_hint: What the project's runs stored in its graph: every deterministic finding at the indexed revision (an index replaces them, so a fixed one leaves), the contradictions the judge confirmed, with both passages, and the other judges' findings. A model's judgment is advisory until its rule is calibrated.
setup_title: Set the project up for the spec graph
setup_hint: The spec-graph service reads the project's first Git source through Studio's Git proxy, at its branch. Say how its documents are laid out.
pulls_hint: Review an open pull request as the spec-graph CI does: the findings it brings (its head against the base below) and the threads CI would post. Review is the deterministic rules, in seconds; With model adds the model's rules (contradictions), minutes and model cost.
no_pulls: No open pull requests in {repository} (as Studio last synced them).
pulls_no_repository: The repository this graph reads is not among the project's sources any more, so its pull requests cannot be told apart from other repositories'. Set the project up again.
pulls_other_repos: Pull requests of the project's other repositories are not listed ({count}): this graph reads {repository} only.
reviewing_model: Reviewing with the model: a run of a few minutes…
review_hint: Studio does not post these on the pull request yet: they are what CI posts, one thread per rule and lines.
review_clean: The pull request brings no finding.
graph_view_hint: The project's spec graph around one node: what points at it on the left, what it points at on the right, a judge's conclusion as a dashed line. Choose a neighbour to centre on it.
graph_hint: Find a node (a requirement, a section, a decision), or open one from a finding with Show in graph.
graph_legend: Left: what points at this node. Right: what it points at. Solid: stated in the documents. Dashed: a judge's conclusion.
setup_layout_gears: Gear directories, each with its own docs/
setup_name_hint: The label these documents carry in the graph and in findings, for example the product's name.
setup_gears_hint: One per line, relative to the repository's root; each gear's documents are under its docs/.
setup_need_gears: name at least one gear directory
ontology_hint: What the spec graph is built of: the node and edge types the service makes of a project's documents, and how many of each this project's graph holds. This is the kit's model of the documents; Studio's Project domain model is another thing.
ontology_unlisted: made by graph-storage (a link's target not yet indexed)
graph_empty: The project's graph is not built yet. Build it with an index run (Build graph above): it reads every document and takes about a minute, with no model.
graph_not_in_graph: This node is not in the project's graph: the graph is not built yet, or the node is gone since the last index run.
graph_picture_truncated: Only part of the graph is drawn: there were more nodes than a picture holds.
status_prepare_hint: Extract the facts of every document and embed them once, so a review with the model then takes a few minutes and cents rather than a quarter of an hour. Minutes and model cost once.
pulls_not_prepared: Model reviews are not prepared: the first review with the model extracts the facts of every document (insight: 16 minutes and $0.57). Prepare them once from the bar above, and a review then takes a few minutes and cents.
ontology_graph_hint: Each node type is a node, sized by how many this project's graph holds; each edge type an edge between the types it connects (a judge's conclusion in purple). Types with 0 appear in later runs: facts and concepts with an index that extracts facts, findings with a contradictions run, the judges' edges with the realization and status judges.
build_facts_hint: Also extract the facts every document states (limits, owners, chosen options) with a model: minutes and model cost, cached, so a re-index pays only for changed pieces. Needed by the contradictions run.
build_contradictions_hint: Then judge the whole corpus for passages that give different values for one thing; the confirmed conflicts are stored as findings (Stored, and on the graph). Minutes and model cost.
setup_build: Build the graph now (structure and deterministic findings, no model)
quality_hint: The project's spec quality in numbers, and how far each rule can be trusted: its precision from people's labels, and whether it has earned the right to block a pull request.
quality_realized_detail: {done} of {count}: a design element realizes them
quality_unlinked_detail: of {pairs} conflicting pairs: authors do not see them side by side
quality_rules_hint: Labels are real / not / unsure. A rule may block once it has {min} labels and the lower bound of its precision is at least {lower}; until then a model's rule only advises.
label: Label…
label_hint: Say whether the finding is real, not a finding, or unsure, with a note: it calibrates the rule and hides nothing.
findings_graph_empty: No finding is stored in the graph yet: an index stores the deterministic ones, a contradictions run the judge's.
quality_graph_hint: Each finding linked to the documents it cites, coloured by rule family; choose a rule in the table to keep only its findings.
quality_show_rule: Show only this rule's findings on the graph below
finding_panel_missing: This finding is no longer stored: index again to see the current ones.
tip_open_depth: Click to open it in Depth →
tip_open_finding: Click to read both passages and decide →
